title: observability: token-level metrics + tracing dashboard and alert tuning
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Enhanced token-level cost and latency dashboards; improved KV-cache tracing; tuned paging and SLO alerts to reduce noisy incidents.
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token cost/latency and KV-cache behavior to reduce noisy alerts and quickly triage production regressions. This PR adds token-level metrics to the observability pipeline, improves tracing spans for KV cache lookups, ships a combined Grafana dashboard for cost/latency/tracing, and tunes alert thresholds to align with recent traffic patterns.

What this PR does: - Adds new token-level counters and histograms (tokens_per_request, token_generation_latency_ms, token_cost_units) emitted from the serving runtime. - Adds KV cache hit/miss/span tracing hooks so traces correlate with token-level metrics. - Introduces a new Grafana dashboard (dashboards/token_level_cost_latency.json) with panels for cost per token, percentile token latencies, KV hit-rate heatmap, and per-model cost breakdown. - Updates alert rules (observability/alerts/token_alerts.yaml) to reduce false positives: raised p95/p99 thresholds, added rate-of-change suppression and a separate alert for sudden token-cost regressions. - Adds docs and quick troubleshooting steps to docs/observability/token-level.md and a quickstart query for the dashboard.

Implementation notes: Emitted metrics use the existing telemetry protobuf and follow the namespacing convention `redwood.serving.token.*`. Tracing uses baggage and sets kv.cache.span attributes so the trace can be linked to token metrics via trace_id. Dashboard panels include links to example traces and to the cost breakdown report in the Console. Alert tuning is conservative: thresholds were derived from a rolling 30-day baseline and validated against canary traffic.

Testing & CI: Unit tests for metrics serialization and an integration test that runs a synthetic workload to generate token-level payloads were added. Local Grafana dashboard was validated against a staging telemetry export.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind obs.token_level.enabled. We'll enable in staging for 48h, run the synthetic workload and run regression queries. If stable, enable in dedicated fleets with a gradual 25/50/100 rollout over 72h.

Related: ENG-4821, ENG-4870, SUP-987.

comments: Ethan Park (review): Nice work. A few nits: can we make the token metric labels include model_version and route? Also please ensure the telemetry proto bump is backwards compatible.
Priya Singh (author): Added model_version and route labels to tokens_per_request and token_cost_units. Kept optional fields in the proto with defaults to preserve compatibility.
Ava Chen (review): Alert tuning looks reasonable. Can we add a short suppression window for deploy spikes (5m) and a runbook link?

Priya Singh (author): Added 5m suppression and linked the new runbook at docs/observability/runbooks/token-cost-regressions.md. Ran the integration workload in staging and observed no noise at the new thresholds.
Diego Morales (approval): Approved. Verified dashboard visualizations and trace links on staging. CI flaky test was re-run and passed. Recommend squash merge.
